TEHRAN- The 21st Tehran-Mobarak International Puppet Theater Festival will open on Saturday with a ceremony at the open-air grounds of Tehran’s City Theater Complex, bringing together puppetry artists and members of the public in a celebration of the art form. For the ceremony, festival secretary Poopak Azimpour Tabrizi has invited artists, students, university professors, theater practitioners and other interested participants to attend with their own puppets, the public relations office of the City Theater Complex announced on Wednesday. The invitation extends to citizens of all ages, highlighting the festival’s effort to encourage public participation and bring puppetry beyond the stage. The opening event will mark the beginning of the six-day festival, which will run in Tehran from October 17 to 22, featuring puppetry performances and activities dedicated to the art form. The Tehran-Mobarak International Puppet Theater Festival is one of Iran’s major cultural events dedicated to puppetry, bringing together Iranian and international artists to showcase different traditions, techniques and approaches to puppet theater. Named after Mobarak, a traditional Iranian glove-puppet character known for his humor and lively exchanges with audiences, the festival celebrates the country’s rich heritage of traditional puppetry while providing a platform for contemporary forms of the art. Its programs highlight puppetry as a medium for storytelling, cultural expression and communication

TEHRAN- The 1987 Iranian film “Where Is the Friend’s House?” by the late acclaimed filmmaker Abbas Kiarostami will be screened at the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival in Japan as part of a special program celebrating films cherished by legendary Japanese director Akira Kurosawa. Produced by the Institute for the Intellectual Development of Children and Young Adults (Kanoon), the film is scheduled to screen on October 26 at TOHO Cinemas Chanter in Tokyo, according to Kanoon’s public relations and international affairs department. The film will be presented alongside three other works in the program “Akira Kurosawa’s Favorite Films”: Charlie Chaplin’s “The Circus” (1928), and Kurosawa’s own films “Sanshiro Sugata” (1943) and “Ikiru” (1952). The special program brings together works associated with Kurosawa’s cinematic legacy, placing Kiarostami’s landmark Iranian film in conversation with major works from the history of world cinema. “Where Is the Friend’s House?” follows Ahmad, a schoolboy who discovers that he has accidentally taken home his classmate’s notebook. Determined to return it before his friend faces punishment for failing to complete his homework, Ahmad sets out to find the boy’s house in a neighboring village. His search becomes a journey through rural Iranian life, exploring childhood, responsibility, kindness and the challenges children encounter in a world governed by adult rules. full_text: Current account surplus in Russia grew to $35 bln in January-August 2026 The foreign trade surplus in goods reached $91.6 bln, up from $73.3 bln in January-August 2025 MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. Russia's current account surplus in January-August 2026 rose to $35 bln against $21 bln in the same period of 2025, according to a preliminary estimate by the Central Bank. The current account surplus in August 2026 amounted to $3.3 bln, compared to a deficit of $0.5 bln last August. The services deficit increased by $2.3 bln compared to the January-August 2025 figure, totaling $33.7 bln. The increase was mainly due to a rise in services imports driven by growing expenses of Russians during trips abroad, and surging costs of transport services provided by nonresidents. The increase in exports was moderate and was primarily supported by transport services, the regulator added. The foreign trade surplus in goods reached $91.6 bln, up from $73.3 bln in January-August 2025, driven by an expansion in exports linked to mounting prices on global commodity markets, the Central Bank said.

full_text: Chinese tourists spend about $1,791 per trip in Russia — study Chinese tourists spend the most on hotels and excursions MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. Chinese tourists spend an average of 150,000 rubles ($1,791) per trip in Russia, according to a joint study by the Association of Tour Operators of Russia (ATOR) and the ExLibris analytical agency seen by TASS. "A total of 150,000 rubles ($1,791) is the median expenditure for a Chinese tourist per trip," the experts noted. According to the study, the travel budget is directly linked to the duration and geography of the trip. In Moscow and St. Petersburg, travel expenses can exceed 100,000-150,000 rubles ($1,194-$1,791) on top of the cost of the tour itself. Meanwhile, the price of tours from China to Lake Baikal and the Primorsky Region ranges from 50,000 to 100,000 rubles ($597-$1,194) per person. Chinese tourists spend the most on hotels and excursions. At the same time, this year has seen a sharp increase in spending on categories such as grocery stores, art museum tickets, and suburban transport, which points to a growing segment of independent travelers.

But the unexploited minerals believed to lie under the vast Arctic island's ground and seabed which could play a crucial role in many new tech and defence industries are also seen as a potential springboard to the territory's independence from Denmark, a goal backed by a majority of the island's 57,000 inhabitants. Greenland has long received subsidies from the Danish government that account for about 20 percent of its economy, and it would need massive investment to survive on its own. Under the proposal adopted Thursday, Greenland's government can extend the moratorium in two-year increments. "With this decision, Greenland has the opportunity to send a strong signal that the protection of the ocean, nature, and our livelihoods must be taken seriously when we are faced with new forms of exploiting marine resources," the WWF said.
